problem:
A particle $P$ of mass $5\,\text{kg}$ is subject to the external forces 

$$
{F}_{1}=⟨\frac{3t-7}{{t}^{2}-1},\,5t⟩,\,{F}_{2}=⟨\frac{7t-3}{{t}^{2}-1},\,5t⟩,
$$

where ${F}_{1}$ and ${F}_{2}$ are measured in Newtons and $t>0$ is the time, in seconds. Given that the velocity of $P$ equals $⟨0,\,-1⟩\,\text{m/s}$ when $t=0\,\text{s},$ calculate the speed of $P$ when $t=1\,\text{s}.$

mathematical_assessment.explanation: Rechecking: for t≠1, F₁+F₂=⟨10(t−1)/(t²−1),10t⟩=⟨10/(t+1),10t⟩. Dividing by 5 and integrating with v(0)=⟨0,−1⟩ gives v(t)=⟨2ln(t+1),t²−1⟩. Its limit at t=1 has speed 2ln(2), matching b. The earlier uncertainty remains: the individual forces are undefined at t=1, and the question does not explicitly specify continuous extension. Option b is justified under that interpretation.
